reason: The cited evidence shows that increasing elements broadens serration temperature range (E1) and that statistical solute fluctuations pin dislocations (E2), but no evidence directly links Co removal to enhanced Cr/Mn fluctuations or to the specific predicted mechanical transitions; E3 and E4 address different alloys or strain-induced ordering, not the proposed mechanism.
premises: Co removal enhances local solute fluctuations (Cr, Mn) that modify stacking fault energies
Solute fluctuations act as dynamic barriers to dislocation motion
At low T/high strain rate, solute obstacles pin dislocations causing serrated flow and enhanced hardening
At high T/low strain rate, thermal activation allows bypass, leading to smooth flow
The Co-free alloy will show increased yield strength and strain rate sensitivity vs. CoCrFeMnNi
